segments.text: We're joined now by Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna of California. Thank you so much for joining us tonight, Congressman. You were, of course, part of the progressive group that met with President Biden at the White House yesterday. The White House called the meetings constructive. So did the president. He expressed urgency as far as getting to a final agreement before he heads overseas next week. And is that timeline realistic, would you say, given where the talks are right now?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Lindsey, we have to meet that timeline. The president spoke about the need for him to go to Glasgow with some deliverables. American leadership is at stake. Our leadership on climate is at stake. He looked at each of us in the eye and he said, "I need this." He appealed to our patriotism. I believe the House will deliver and the Senate will deliver.
And

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: let's talk numbers here. Are progressives now willing to accept that this final package will be somewhere between one and a quarter and two trillion dollars? Can House Democrats even sign on to that level if the spending is put on priorities that you can all agree on?
It's still

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_12
segments.text: ongoing negotiations. I don't want to give a specific

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: number, but I will say that the House progressives recognize that there will be significant cuts, that many of these

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_15
segments.text: programs aren't going to be 10 years, and that we have to compromise. And the reality is we

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_15

paid

you can't agree

segments.text: But on paid family leave, I don't think four weeks is enough. I think anyone who knows someone who has been pregnant will tell you that four weeks isn't enough. So we're pushing back to say, let's have something more realistic, even if we have to have less years. For the child tax credit, what is most important is that we don't means test that beyond the American Rescue Plan. But the big issue for progressives is climate change.
